title: The denied refusal leaves a --json caller with no migration receipt and a hint it cannot act on
description:
Found by an adversarial reviewer during PR #140 (LCLI-467). The exit code itself is CORRECT and is not in question: cli-contract section 5.1 defines 4 / denied as "the operation is refused: e.g. a guarded destructive op without the required confirmation", an exact fit, and error_type denied maps to exit 4 per 5.3. Stream discipline is correct too (stdout empty on failure, section 4).

TWO THINGS THAT ARE NOT COHERENT:

1. THE MACHINE CALLER LOSES THE MIGRATION RECEIPT. Section 4's invariant means stdout is empty on exit 4, and the error envelope's `input` carries only {reason}. So a caller that ran `--migrate-backlog --remove-backlog` and got exit 4 cannot read the digest, mappings, survivors or task fingerprints of a migration that DID apply. docs/reference/cli-surface.md's new paragraph says "the migration itself still stands" -- true of the repository, but not recoverable from the envelope. Adding migrationDigest / migrationApplied to `input` is permitted as additive under section 7.1 and would close it.

2. THE HINT IS NOT ACTIONABLE. It says "commit or clean backlog/ ... then rerun", but a rerun of `lore init --tracker quest --migrate-backlog --remove-backlog` re-enters runBacklogMigration and the records are already in Quest. There is no removal-only entry point in the CLI surface, so the only clean recoveries are "commit the deletion by hand" or "clean backlog/ and hope the second migration is idempotent". PLAUSIBLE rather than confirmed -- the reviewer did not drive a real double migration.

Fix shape: either a removal-only entry point, or a hint that says what to actually do. Decide which; do not just reword.
plan: 1. Item 1 (sanctioned, additive per section 7.1): carry migrationDigest + migrationApplied on the DENIED --remove-backlog refusal input, asserted on the existing stub (test/init.test.ts:3536).

2. Measurement (leader-requested): a REAL double migration in a temp repo OUTSIDE the repo -- exit code, stdout/stderr of the SECOND run, whether it re-migrates / refuses / no-ops; plus whether ANY existing command or flag combination today completes ONLY the backlog removal after a migration applied.
3. Report the evidence; item 2s arm (hint vs removal-only entry point) is opum-docs call. No PR and no review until the arm is chosen.
implementationNotes: Completed on branch fix/LCLI-525-denied-receipt-and-hint, per opum-doc DEC-172 (4af) (relay 571, 15:22:58Z). ITEM 1: the denied --remove-backlog refusal input now carries migrationDigest + migrationApplied (additive, section 7.1), asserted in the existing refusal test. ITEM 2, ARM A: the hint no longer promises a rerun as the way to finish the REMOVAL; it now reads "there is no removal-only path after an applied migration: rerun WITHOUT --remove-backlog to keep backlog/ (a verified removal is not available yet), or delete backlog/ by hand -- which skips the verified archive .lore/archive/backlog-<digest>.zip". No removal-only entry point in this job. WHY THE OLD HINT WAS WRONG -- MEASURED, not inferred (real double migration, temp repo OUTSIDE the repo): RUN 1 = denied exit 4 with the migration APPLIED (3 Quest records); the hinted rerun = type=CONFLICT EXIT 5 (alias collision against the aliases the first run created), whether backlog/ was DIRTY (run 2) or CLEAN (run 3); and --remove-backlog without --migrate-backlog is a usage refusal, so no existing command completes only the removal. The rerun defect is filed UNSTAMPED as LCLI-699, carrying opum-docs direction verbatim plus the run 2 / run 3 evidence, and NOT implemented. TESTS: the refusal test now asserts the new hint text AND that it no longer contains the old rerun promise (not "then rerun", not "git checkout -- backlog/"); flipping WITHOUT to WITH reddens it (1 fail). DOCS: cli-surface.md now records the receipt fields and that no removal-only path exists yet. GATES: full suite 4986 tests / 2 skip / 0 fail; lint, typecheck and lore check green.
finalSummary: Two incoherences on the denied --remove-backlog refusal are closed, per opum-doc DEC-172 (4af) (arm A). (1) The receipt is no longer lost to a --json caller: the refusal input carries migrationDigest and migrationApplied (additive, section 7.1), since stdout is byte-empty on exit 4 and input is the only channel. (2) The hint no longer promises a rerun, which MEASUREMENT showed cannot work: a real double migration gave denied / exit 4 on run 1 with the migration applied, then type=CONFLICT / EXIT 5 (alias collision against the first run aliases) on the hinted rerun -- whether backlog/ was dirty or clean -- and no removal-only path exists. The hint now names the one safe recovery (rerun WITHOUT --remove-backlog, keeping backlog/), says a verified removal after an applied migration is not available yet, and warns that a hand deletion skips the verified archive. Tests assert the new text and that the old rerun promise is gone, mutation-verified. The rerun defect is filed unstamped as LCLI-699, not implemented. Full suite 4986 tests / 2 skip / 0 fail; lint, typecheck and lore check green. Run job-0tuyqhv.
